description: PROTOCOL_SPEC §9.2.1 — the closed set of path-typed configuration keys. A path-typed key is one whose value is a filesystem path; the set is declared by `"x-apcore-path": true` in schemas/apcore-config.schema.json (and mirrored in schemas/defaults.schema.json for the three keys that carry defaults there). This fixture exists because the set was previously undeclared, so every consumer that needed it built its own: apcore-cli hand-maintained SANDBOX_PATH_TYPED_VARS with a note that adding a key means editing three SDKs, and nothing detected drift between that list and the schemas. SCOPE: this fixture asserts WHICH keys are path-typed and that each SDK exposes the set. It asserts NOTHING about what a relative value resolves against — the resolution base is unspecified as of spec v1.34.0 and tracked in issue #113. A driver that starts asserting resolved absolute paths here is testing an undecided question.

driver_contract.accessor: Each driver supplies its SDK's public path-typed key accessor (apcore-python `Config.path_typed_keys()`, apcore-typescript `Config.pathTypedKeys()`, apcore-rust `Config::path_typed_keys()`). The accessor MUST be public API — a private constant that happens to hold the right values does not satisfy §9.2.1 requirement 1, because the consumer this set exists for lives in another repository.
driver_contract.comparison: Compare as a SET, not a sequence — ordering is not normative. Report the symmetric difference (missing keys AND extra keys) rather than a boolean: an SDK that omits one key and invents another passes any length check.
driver_contract.both_directions_required: A driver MUST assert both directions. Asserting only 'every expected key is present' passes an implementation that marks every config key as path-typed, which is exactly as wrong as marking none and strictly harder to notice.
driver_contract.roots_element_form: `extensions.roots` is list-valued and both element forms are path-typed (bare string, and the {root, namespace} object). Drivers report the key as `extensions.roots[]` regardless of which form a given element uses; an SDK that models only one form is reported as a violation of the `extensions.roots[]` entry, not as a separate key.

test_cases.comment: The projection of `x-apcore-path` markers out of the canonical schemas equals `path_typed_keys` above. This case guards the fixture itself against drifting from the schemas it claims to project.
Symmetric difference between the SDK accessor and the declared set MUST be empty.

DISCRIMINATING CASE. `bindings.pattern` sits in the same config section as `bindings.dir`, carries a filesystem-looking default (`*.binding.yaml`), and is the most likely key to be swept in by an implementation that classifies by section or by 'looks like a filename'. §9.2.1 requirement 4 states it is a glob matched against filenames WITHIN `bindings.dir`, never resolved as a path itself.
Second discriminating case: string-valued keys that are not paths. An implementation that marks every string key as path-typed fails here and passes every presence-only assertion.
Both element forms of the list carry paths.
§9.2.1 requirement 3 — an implementation MUST NOT invent a delimiter-separated scalar encoding for the list-valued key. Setting APCORE_EXTENSIONS_ROOTS MUST NOT produce a two-element roots list.
The set is a property of the specification, not of a loaded document. A Config built from defaults and a Config loaded from a file that sets none of these keys MUST report the same set.
